key_insight: In strongly turbulent anisotropic magnetic fields, high-energy particle scattering is not controlled by the turbulence correlation length, and adding a guide field reveals a different-than-expected scattering mechanism.
engineering_relevance: This changes how we model particle transport in space and astrophysical plasmas, especially when turbulence is strong and a mean magnetic field is weak or absent.
method: Generated realistic 3D turbulent magnetic field realizations with the BxC toolkit.
Simulated high-energy particle transport in anisotropic strong-turbulence cases.
Compared scattering behavior with and without a guide magnetic field.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports observed evidence from synthetic-field particle transport experiments, including a verification study with a guide field showing behavior inconsistent with standard correlation-length and pitch-angle diffusion expectations.
watch_item: Because the results come from synthetic turbulent realizations, their applicability to specific astrophysical environments may depend on how well the generated fields match real plasma conditions.
paper_title: High-energy Particle Transport in Three-dimensional Anisotropic Turbulent Magnetic Fields
